concepts.title: Displacement Relation in a Progressive Wave
concepts.definition: A mathematical function representing the displacement of particles in a medium as a function of both spatial position and time during wave propagation.
concepts.formula: y = a * sin(k * x - omega * t + phi)
concepts.key_idea: Describes a sinusoidal wave travelling in space and time with a specific amplitude, wave number, and frequency.
question_patterns: calculate the amplitude, wavelength, and frequency of the wave
find the displacement of the wave at a given distance and time
determine the angular wave number and angular frequency from the wave equation
what is the wavelength of a progressive wave with wave number

solution_steps.explain: Wavelength is 2 * pi divided by the angular wave number k
Frequency is angular frequency divided by 2 * pi

concepts.title: Speed of a Travelling Wave
concepts.definition: The speed at which any given phase point of a wave propagates through the supporting material medium.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, the wave pattern shifts a distance equal to one wavelength in the duration of one time period.
question_patterns: calculate the speed of a travelling wave given wavelength and frequency
find the wavelength of a wave given its speed and frequency
what is the frequency of a wave with speed and wavelength
how far does a wave travel in a given time period

solution_steps.explain: Multiply wavelength by frequency to find the speed of propagation

concepts.title: Speed of a Transverse Wave on a Stretched String
concepts.definition: The propagation speed of a transverse disturbance along a tensioned string, determined by the tension and linear mass density.
concepts.key_idea: Speed increases with tension and decreases with heavier strings (higher linear mass density).
question_patterns: calculate the speed of transverse waves on a wire under tension
find the tension required in a steel wire to achieve a certain wave speed
what is the speed of a wave on a string of mass and length under tension
how long does a disturbance take to reach the other end of a stretched string

solution_steps.explain: Divide total mass by length of the string
Take the square root of tension divided by linear mass density

concepts.title: Speed of a Longitudinal Wave in Solids and Fluids
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, the speed of compressional waves in a medium, determined by its bulk modulus (for fluids) or Young's modulus (for solid bars) and its density.
concepts.key_idea: Speed of sound varies with the elastic modulus and mass density of the medium.
question_patterns: calculate the speed of longitudinal waves in a solid bar
find the speed of sound in a fluid given bulk modulus and density
determine the speed of a longitudinal wave in steel
what is the speed of sound in a metal rod

solution_steps.explain: Take the square root of elastic modulus divided by mass density

concepts.title: Speed of Sound in an Ideal Gas
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the speed of sound in a gas under adiabatic conditions, incorporating the ratio of specific heats (Laplace's correction).
concepts.key_idea: Sound propagation in gas is an adiabatic process, not isothermal.
question_patterns: estimate the speed of sound in air at standard temperature and pressure
calculate the speed of sound in a gas using Laplace correction
find the speed of sound given pressure, density, and adiabatic index
how does the speed of sound in air change with temperature

solution_steps.action: Calculate speed of sound in gas
solution_steps.explain: Take the square root of gamma times pressure divided by density

concepts.title: Superposition and Interference of Waves
concepts.definition: In brief, the principle stating that the net displacement of a medium where multiple waves overlap is indeed the algebraic sum of their individual displacements.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Overlapping waves of the same frequency produce a resultant wave whose amplitude varies with their phase difference.
question_patterns: calculate the resultant amplitude of two waves with phase difference
find the amplitude of the combined wave when phase difference is
what is the amplitude of the wave resulting from superposition
explain constructive and destructive interference of waves

solution_steps.explain: Find the phase difference phi between the two interfering waves
If phase difference is an even multiple of pi, it is constructive; if an odd multiple, it is destructive

concepts.title: Standing Waves on a Stretched String
concepts.definition: Stationary wave patterns formed by the superposition of two identical waves travelling in opposite directions on a string fixed at both ends.
concepts.key_idea: Boundary conditions restrict the allowed frequencies to integer multiples of the fundamental frequency.
question_patterns: calculate the fundamental frequency of a stretched string
find the frequency of the nth harmonic of a wire fixed at both ends
what is the speed of a transverse wave on a string vibrating in its fundamental mode
calculate the tension in a string vibrating at a given frequency

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the harmonic number by wave speed and divide by twice the length

concepts.title: Standing Waves in a Closed Organ Pipe
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Resonant normal modes of an air column in a pipe closed at one both x and y open at the other, producing only odd harmonics.
concepts.key_idea: The closed end is a displacement node and the open end is an antinode, restricting the modes to odd harmonics.
question_patterns: calculate the fundamental frequency of a pipe closed at one end
find the resonant frequencies of a closed organ pipe
which harmonic of a closed pipe resonates with a source
what is the length of a closed pipe resonating at a given frequency

solution_steps.action: Calculate resonant frequency of closed pipe
solution_steps.explain: Multiply the odd harmonic factor (2*n + 1) by speed and divide by four times the length

concepts.title: Standing Waves in an Open Organ Pipe
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Resonant normal modes of an air column in a pipe open at both ends, producing all integer harmonics.
concepts.key_idea: Both ends are displacement antinodes, allowing all harmonic frequencies.
question_patterns: calculate the fundamental frequency of an open organ pipe
find the harmonic mode of an open pipe that resonates with a source
what is the length of an open pipe resonating at a given frequency
will resonance be observed if one end of the open pipe is closed

solution_steps.action: Calculate resonant frequency of open pipe
solution_steps.explain: Multiply the harmonic number by speed and divide by twice the length

concepts.title: Beat Frequency
concepts.definition: The periodic variation in intensity heard when two sound waves of slightly different frequencies interfere.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, the beat frequency equals the absolute difference between the two interfering frequencies.
question_patterns: calculate the beat frequency produced by two tuning forks
find the frequency of a sitar string given the beat frequency
what is the beat frequency when two waves of frequencies are heard together
determine the original frequency of a string from a change in beat frequency

solution_steps.explain: Take the absolute difference between the two frequencies

worked_examples.question_pattern: A wave travelling along a string is described by y(x, t) = {amplitude_val} sin ({k_val} x - {omega_val} t). Calculate the amplitude, wavelength, and frequency.

solution_template.explain: The coefficient of the sine term is the amplitude
Wavelength is 2 * pi divided by the wave number k
Frequency is angular frequency divided by 2 * pi

worked_examples.question_pattern: A steel wire {length} m long has a mass of {mass} kg. If the wire is under a tension of {tension} N, what is the speed of transverse waves on the wire?

extracted_variables.length: length of the wire in meters
extracted_variables.mass: mass of the wire in kg
extracted_variables.tension: tension in the wire in Newtons

solution_template.explain: Divide total mass by length of the string
Take the square root of tension divided by linear mass density

worked_examples.question_pattern: Two sitar strings A and B produce beats of frequency {beat_freq} Hz. When tension of B is slightly increased, the beat frequency decreases to {new_beat_freq} Hz. If the frequency of A is {freq_A} Hz, find the original frequency of B.

extracted_variables.freq_A: frequency of string A in Hz

solution_template.explain: Since increasing tension of B increases its frequency and decreases the beat frequency, B's original frequency must be lower than A's.
